subject: Day 55: pre-fill 24h of feeds
bodyText:
Today's focus
Today is logistics prep ahead of the 2-month visit, which opens tomorrow. The single highest-leverage move is buffering the next day of feeds so post-vaccine fussiness does not collide with an empty bottle.

Action items
- Pre-fill the next 24 hours of breastmilk or formula and stage it in the fridge, since vaccine fussiness reliably disrupts the feeding rhythm for a day or two. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Confirm tomorrow's appointment time and bring a printed question list: sleep-training stance, solids timing, growth percentile trajectory, and when to drop the swaddle. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Stage infant acetaminophen but do not dose before the shots; treat fever after, since pre-dosing can blunt the antibody response. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Drooling and wet sneezes from salivary-gland maturation, plus occasional hiccups after feeds; none require action.
- [monitor] No social smile by eight weeks (Avi is 55 days, just under): note it now and raise it at tomorrow's visit.
- [call within 24h] Forceful arching during feeds with painful spit-up, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, blue lips, labored breathing, or a seizure-like episode; for blue lips call 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Sing or play a short Suzuki recording during a calm wake window; early listening exposure builds the perceptual base before formal lessons begin. Suzuki Association: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Read the same favorite board book aloud to anchor the day with familiar rhythm; predictable repetition is the active ingredient pre-verbally. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Run tummy time as four to six short bouts toward 45 to 60 minutes total, staggered across the day rather than one long session. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold him at a mirror for two to three minutes; self-recognition is months away, but the face circuitry is actively calibrating now.

Upcoming
- Day 56-70 (now open): 2-month well visit. Vaccines due: HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48h window. Expect fussiness, low-grade fever, and extra sleep.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit. Vaccines: RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
